source: Coordinates from each Wikipedia article (GeoData) or Wikidata P625; text is short editorial context.

features.name: Grand Canyon
features.why: Carved by the Colorado River over millions of years; about a mile deep.

features.name: Glen Canyon
features.why: Mostly drowned by Lake Powell when Glen Canyon Dam closed in 1963.

features.name: Black Canyon of the Gunnison
features.why: Sheer, narrow gorge cut by the Gunnison River, a Colorado tributary.

features.name: Death Valley
features.why: Lowest, hottest and driest place in North America; a closed basin.

features.name: Mojave Desert
features.why: Driest desert in North America; Las Vegas sits on its northeastern edge.

features.name: Sonoran Desert
features.why: Saguaro desert around Phoenix and Tucson, watered by the CAP and the Salt–Verde system.

features.name: Great Basin Desert
features.why: Cold desert where every river ends in a lake or sink instead of the sea.

features.name: Sierra Nevada
features.why: Its snowpack is California’s biggest reservoir.

features.name: Wasatch Range
features.why: Snowmelt from here supplies the Wasatch Front, from Provo to Ogden.

features.name: Uinta Mountains
features.why: Rare east–west range; the Central Utah Project tunnels its water west.

features.name: Mogollon Rim
features.why: Escarpment where the Salt and Verde rivers begin, feeding Phoenix.

features.name: Imperial Valley
features.why: Former desert below sea level, irrigated entirely with Colorado River water.

features.name: Central Valley
features.why: Among the world’s most productive farm regions, fed by both state and federal canals.

features.name: Arches
features.why: Sandstone arches near Moab, above the Colorado River.

features.name: Canyonlands
features.why: Where the Green River meets the Colorado.

features.name: Zion
features.why: Canyon cut by the Virgin River, upstream of St. George.
